Context · what Sibyl reads

        
The eight deal readings, the fixed components the calculator settled
           (01 Closed Won, 05 Create & Close), the top-down metrics, the forecast history and rep
           accuracy for this week of quarter, the decisions log — and both policy files.
           Not the raw deal records: Sibyl is the manager here, not the deal reader.

Review · approve, edit, escalate

        

          

          

             
             

          
The three buttons wake up as soon as an agent output exists.


          

            
Edit the draft. This is Sibyl's submission text. Change what you need,
               then Save — your version becomes the version of record and the change is written into
               the run log.

            

            

               

          


          

            
Escalate. One line: why this run does not get a decision from you.
               The reason is the record.

            
            

            

               

          


          

          

        


        
Maya replies — back to Sibyl

        
Push back, ask for a change, or test the boundary. Sibyl answers on the same
           conversation. Sibyl cannot submit to the VP — asking it to is refused
           under M8.1. A reply is itself a human action: it is logged, and the gate re-opens on
           Sibyl's answer.

        

        

        

        
Nothing is sent without human approval.

      


      
      

        
        


        
Five cases from my PRD. Expected is my own row, word for
           word. Actual is what the agent did on a real run, quoted — never a
           summary of Expected. Verdict is mine: the agent does not grade itself.

        
EC-1, EC-3 and EC-4 are three questions about one weekly forecast, so
           Run scores the current run when there is one and says which run it used. Fresh run forces
           a new one. EC-2 always runs with its source withheld; EC-5 answers a draft, so run EC-1
           first.
